title: medDreamer: Model-Based Reinforcement Learning with Latent Imagination on Complex EHRs for Clinical Decision Support

problem.claim: Clinical decision support must handle personalized treatment decisions for patient responses that vary and evolve over time, using irregularly sampled clinical data.

gap.claim: Existing RL-based clinical decision support systems often ignore informative missingness, distort irregular data through coarse discretization and simple imputation, and rely predominantly on model-free learning from retrospective data.

contributions.claim: The authors propose medDreamer, a model-based reinforcement learning framework for personalized treatment recommendation with a world model, an Adaptive Feature Integration module for irregular data, and a two-phase policy trained on real and imagined trajectories.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe medDreamer as a novel model-based reinforcement learning framework for personalized treatment recommendation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report evaluating medDreamer on sepsis and mechanical ventilation treatment tasks using two large-scale EHR datasets.
The authors report that medDreamer significantly outperforms model-free and model-based baselines in clinical outcomes and off-policy metrics.

narrative_sequence.summary: Personalized and timely treatment decisions are needed because patient responses vary and change over time.
Clinical data are irregularly sampled, and missingness patterns may contain information about patient condition.
Existing clinical RL systems may mishandle irregularity and missingness and may inherit exploration and behavioral biases from retrospective model-free learning.
medDreamer combines latent patient-state simulation from irregular data with policy training over real and imagined trajectories.
The authors evaluate the framework on sepsis and mechanical ventilation tasks and report improvements over baselines.

source_observation.claim: Missing-data frequencies in irregular clinical records may implicitly convey information about patient condition.

interpretation.claim: Data absence patterns can be treated as potentially informative signals rather than only as nuisances requiring imputation.

application.claim: When modeling irregular longitudinal records, preserve or explicitly model missingness patterns before applying discretization or imputation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that missingness is informative in every clinical setting or dataset.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, cohort sizes, preprocessing details, model architecture beyond the named modules, or training hyperparameters.
The abstract does not provide numerical effect sizes, uncertainty estimates, or details of the off-policy metrics.
The abstract does not establish independent verification, clinical deployment feasibility, or prospective patient benefit.
